intelligence_brief.title: Semiconductor Supply Chain and Critical Mineral Geopolitical Assessment

Taiwan.developments: TSMC continues to accelerate 2nm node production timelines amidst heightened cross-strait military posturing. Supply chain resilience protocols have been activated to mitigate potential maritime blockade risks.
Taiwan.critical_minerals: Stable supply of neon gas and photoresists, though stockpiling remains at 180-day capacity.

Japan.developments: Rapid expansion of Rapidus Corporation facilities in Hokkaido. Government subsidies are prioritizing domestic logic chip manufacturing to reduce reliance on external foundries.
Japan.critical_minerals: Increased investment in rare earth element recycling technologies to decouple from Chinese export quotas.

United_States.developments: CHIPS Act funding tranches are being deployed to Arizona and Ohio hubs. Focus remains on securing domestic packaging and assembly capabilities to close the backend manufacturing gap.
United_States.critical_minerals: Department of Energy initiatives are fast-tracking lithium and cobalt extraction projects in Nevada and Maine to secure EV and semiconductor battery supply chains.

European_Union.developments: The EU Chips Act is driving cross-border investment in German and French fabrication sites. Focus is on automotive-grade chips to support the transition to electric mobility.
European_Union.critical_minerals: Critical Raw Materials Act implementation is underway, focusing on diversifying supply from Australia and Canada to mitigate dependency on non-aligned suppliers.

Action: US President Donald Trump says he will charge vessels a 20% tax to cross the Strait of Hormuz under the watch of US forces. The claim has been met with bafflement in the shipping industry - not least because it’s far more than Iran planned to charge ships before the ceasefire. Iran would have charged the operator of a very large crude carrier (VLCC) the equivalent of $2 per barrel. A VLCC carries about two million barrels, so that could be $4 million per vessel - but few firms are thought to have paid the so-called ‘Tehran tollbooth’. Trump’s plan would far exceed that, costing tens of millions of dollars. 'With current Brent price ($76), that’s $16 a barrel will go to Trump', said Amena Bak

The southern route is designated by Oman and the UN to keep vessels away from Iranian mines and its hostile navy.
